comment: The section provides a strong definition of governance but does not clearly distinguish governance of the national digital-health architecture from governance of individual DPI-H components, shared data assets, standards, and operational services. These levels involve different decision rights and accountable bodies.

public.text: The section provides a strong definition of governance but does not clearly distinguish governance of the national digital-health architecture from governance of individual DPI-H components, shared data assets, standards, and operational services. These levels involve different decision rights and accountable bodies.
public.suggestedRevision: Introduce a governance-level model covering: national digital-health architecture governance; DPI-H portfolio governance; component governance; data and semantic governance; and operational service governance. Explain how decisions and escalations move between these levels.
